To convert a grade to a percentage, you can use the formulas and tables below depending on what type of grade you have (points, letter grade, or GPA). 

If you want an instant calculation, **simply reply with your grade (e.g., "18 out of 24", "B+", or "3.4 GPA") and I will calculate it for you!**

---

### 1. Point-Based Grade to Percentage (e.g., 18 out of 25)
If you have a test or assignment score, use this simple formula:

$$\text{Percentage (\%)} = \left( \frac{\text{Your Score}}{\text{Total Possible Score}} \right) \times 100$$

*   **Example:** You got **17** out of **22** on a quiz.
    *   $\frac{17}{22} = 0.7727$
    *   $0.7727 \times 100 =$ **$77.27\%$** (a C+)

---

### 2. Letter Grade to Percentage (Standard US Scale)
*Note: Grading scales vary by school, but this is the most common standard used in the US:*

| Letter Grade | Percentage Range | Midpoint Percentage | GPA (4.0 Scale) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **A+** | 97% – 100% | 98.5% | 4.0 |
| **A** | 93% – 96% | 94.5% | 4.0 |
| **A-** | 90% – 92% | 91.0% | 3.7 |
| **B+** | 87% – 89% | 88.0% | 3.3 |
| **B** | 83% – 86% | 84.5% | 3.0 |
| **B-** | 80% – 82% | 81.0% | 2.7 |
| **C+** | 77% – 79% | 78.0% | 2.3 |
| **C** | 73% – 76% | 74.5% | 2.0 |
| **C-** | 70% – 72% | 71.0% | 1.7 |
| **D+** | 67% – 69% | 68.0% | 1.3 |
| **D** | 65% – 66% | 65.5% | 1.0 |
| **F** | Below 65% | 50.0% | 0.0 |

---

### 3. GPA to Percentage (4.0 Scale)
To convert a cumulative GPA on a 4.0 scale back to an approximate percentage, you can use this standard high school conversion formula:

$$\text{Percentage (\%)} = (\text{GPA} \times 20) + 20$$

*   **Example:** You have a **3.4 GPA**.
    *   $(3.4 \times 20) + 20$
    *   $68 + 20 =$ **$88\%$** (a B+)

*(Note: This formula is most accurate for GPAs of 1.0 and higher).*

---
